How the calculation works

Visit cost = (cleaning hours + paid travel/setup hours) × cleaners × loaded hourly cost + supplies + allocated overhead. Loaded hourly cost = wage × (1 + labor burden / 100). Quote = visit cost ÷ (1 − target margin / 100).

Hours are elapsed hours per cleaner. Two cleaners working three hours means six person-hours. Monthly visits are entered explicitly: weekly service is not always four visits per month. Sales tax / VAT is excluded.

Use actual payroll and expense records. Labor burden should cover the employer costs you choose to allocate, such as benefits and payroll costs. Do not count the same expense again in overhead. This model does not determine a market price or calculate tax.

Worked example

Two cleaners × (3 cleaning hours + 0.5 travel/setup hours) × 22.50 loaded hourly cost + 12 supplies + 25 overhead = 194.50 cost per visit. At 25% target margin, the quote is 259.33 before tax. A 25% cleaning-time overrun raises costs to 228.25, leaving 31.08 before any discount.

Methodology reviewed 7 October 2026

Common questions

Is margin the same as markup?

No. A 25% margin on a cost of 100 requires a price of 133.33. A 25% markup gives 125 and a 20% margin.

Are VAT and local payroll rates included?

No. Enter your own costs and add the applicable tax separately. Country selection sets currency; it does not apply local tax law.

Are these default figures market rates?

No. All defaults are an illustrative example. Replace them with your own payroll, expenses and measured time.

Does changing currency convert my quote?

No. The symbol and formatting change, but the entered amounts remain the same.
